sections.title: Why Study Dentistry in France?
sections.lead: For students who want to study Dentistry in France, it is a great option. French dental education offers a blend of scientific basis, clinical training, supervised patient care and opportunities for advanced specialisation.

items: The French dental degree is the Diplôme d'État de docteur en chirurgie dentaire (Doctor of Dental Surgery).
Students who complete the required education and meet professional registration requirements can become a dental surgeon in France.

groups.text: Main advantages of studying dentistry in France are:

items: A university-based dental education system structured.
Education in dental anatomy, diagnosis, treatment and oral health.
Clinical learning and supervised practical experience.
Possibility of specialization in areas like orthodontics, oral surgery and oral medicine.
Admission to public universities where tuition and registration fees could be relatively cheaper depending on the student's fee category.
Possibilities for dental practice, academic and research once the licensing requirements are met.
Through Edu Hawk worldwide study abroad advice students can get to know about these opportunities and the requirements involved in pursuing education overseas.

sections.title: Dentistry Courses in France
sections.lead: France's dental education is not structured around the \\BDS or DDS degrees\\ that are common in many other countries.

items: PASS or L.AS: Health Studies, First Year
Usually students who want to join the dentistry profession have two paths:
PASS (\Parcours d'accès spécifique santé\):\\ First year in health, with additional academic study.
L.AS (\Licence avec accès santé\):\\ A university degree program that includes a health-access component.

To be eligible to gain admission to \\odontologie\\, the French dental program, students must fulfill the relevant \\progression and selection requirements\. Completion of PASS or L.AS does not ensure admission to dentistry.
Dental Studies: Dentistry
After getting admitted, students study subjects such as:
Dental anatomy and oral biology.
Human anatomy and physiology.
Oral pathology and microbiology.
Dental materials and restorative dentistry
Endodontics and periodontology
Prosthodontics.
Oral Diagnosis and Preventive Dentistry
Clinical practice and patient managemen
Graduate Dental Education
Following the completion of the appropriate stages of dental education and selection requirements, students can undertake further training in \\specialist dental areas\.
How long does it take to study dentistry in France
The usual route to the French state dental qualification takes around six years - the first year of health access and then dental training .
Specialist training - usually means additional years in training, depending on the specialty.

sections.title: Eligibility to study dentistry in France?
sections.lead: Your eligibility will depend on your \\previous education, nationality, language proficiency\\ and the entry point you intend to take.

items: For students applying after secondary school the normal starting point is a qualification equivalent to the \\French baccalauréat\\ which gives entry to higher education.

Indian applicants will generally be asked to provide their \\Class 12 results\\ and such other documents as needed for the particular application route. If you are well prepared \\science subjects\\ are especially useful, particularly \\biology, chemistry and physics\.
French Language proficiency\\
The majority of dental teaching and \\clinical communication\\ is in French and applicants need a high level of \\French proficiency\.
Depending on the university and the application route, you may need to provide a recognized \\French-language certificate\\ such as \\DELF, DALF or TCF\.
Good communication skills are required for clinical training and some programs may require \\B2 or C1-level proficiency.\\
Applicants may also be expected to demonstrate:
Academic preparation for demanding \\health sciences studies.
The capacity to satisfy \\university entrance and progression requirements.
The financial means to cover living expenses and tuition.
Have the appropriate \\French student visa or residence permission.

sections.title: Admission requirements Dentistry in France
sections.lead: Dentistry in France admission is competitive and submitted to specific rules of the French higher education system.

items: Post Class 12 Students Applying\\
The way in which students apply to start their first year of health studies usually depends on their nationality, where they live and what their secondary school qualification is.
For eligible international candidates, this could be the \\Études en France platform\\ and the \\preliminary admission process\\ known as \\DAP\\ or another prescribed route.
Students Currently Studying Dentistry\\

Applicants who have started \\dental studies in another country\\ should not expect to be able to transfer directly into a later year of French odontologie. \\Transfers, credit for studies already completed and possible exemptions\\ are governed by the particular rules and decisions of the institution.

sections.title: Cost of studying dentistry in France
sections.lead: The \\cost of dental education in France\\ depends on the university, the level of study, the student's nationality or fee category and any exemption from differentiated fees.

items: Published standard public-university registration fees for the \\2026-2027 academic year\\ are:
State dental qualification and some later-cycle registrations\\ \| Standard rate shown normally €255 per year \|

These are \\standard published registration rates, not a guaranteed total fee for each international student\. \\Non-EU students\\ may be subject to \\differentiated fees, exemptions or other applicable arrangements\. Universities can also impose other fees approved.
\Cost of living\\
\\Cost of living in France\\ Cost of living depends on the city, accommodation and lifestyle.
Students might expect \\€800–€1,400 per month\\ as a rough first planning estimate, with Paris generally more expensive than smaller university cities.
However, they are estimates, not official tariffs. \\Accommodation deposits, insurance, travel\\ and other one-off costs can increase the initial budget.

sections.title: Admission Procedure to Dentistry in France
sections.lead: The \\application process for dentistry in France\\ will differ depending on whether you are applying straight out of school, transferring from another institution or looking for recognition of an existing dental qualification.

items: For a student applying post-Class 12, the process generally includes:
1. \\ Research dental universities \\ Find schools that offer \\ odontologie \\ Check their admission procedures .
2. \\Check eligibility:\\ Check requirements for secondary-school qualifications, language standards and application deadlines.

items.title: Find the right platform: In India, students usually have to check the applicable \\Études en France procédure via Campus France India.
items.desc: 4. \\Application preparation:\\ Gather academic records, language certificates, identity documents and other required evidence.

items: 5. \\Submission of application:\\ Follow the instructions of the respective platform and select the suitable study pathway.
6. \\Complete any necessary selection steps\\: Follow university instructions for assessment, admission or progression.
7. \\Admission decision:\\ Look for the conditions and deadlines listed in the offer.
8. \\Arrange funding:\\ Confirm \\tuition fees, living expenses\\ and evidence of funds.
9. \\Apply for a student visa:\\ Follow the official \\French student visa process\\ relevant to your situation.
10. \\Finalize your university registration:\\ Submit your required paperwork and enrolll administratively before classes start.
8. \\How Does Accreditation and Recognition Work for Dentistry in France?
Students must follow the required curriculum and sit the necessary exams to be eligible to gain the qualification.

However, graduating from a dental program and being \\licensed to practice\\ are two different things. \\Professional registration\\ and other requirements must be fulfilled before a person can practice as a dentist.
\\Recognition in other countries\\
If you plan to return to India or practice in another country, you should check the rules of the relevant \\dental regulator\\ \\before you enrol\.
Recognition may depend on the country, the institution, the qualification, the structure of clinical training and any licensing examinations or registration procedures required.
9. \\Dentists Salary & Job Opportunities in France\\

Graduates who have achieved the necessary qualifications and fulfilled the relevant \\professional registration requirements\\ can seek \\dental careers in France\\ and overseas, subject to the local regulations.
Opportunities
General dentists.
\\Dentist in a dental office or medical office.
\\Dental specialist\\ following recognized additional training .
\\Dental academic or research professional.
\\Oral health educator or public health professional\\ if suitably qualified.
\\Dental sector jobs\\ in research, education or industry.
Expectations on Salary\\
\\Earnings of dentists in France\\ vary greatly depending on experience, location, employment arrangement, working hours, specialization and whether the dentist is employed or self-employed.
Do Foreign Students Have the Right to Work in France?\\

Graduating doesn't mean you automatically get unlimited \\work rights\. International graduates also need to satisfy the \\professional registration requirements for dentistry\\ and the \\immigration conditions\\ that apply to their circumstances.

faqs.q: Can Indian students pursue dentistry in France after Class 12?
faqs.a: Yes, \\Indian students can look for applications to French higher education\\ but they need to fulfill the \\academic, language, admission and visa criteria. They must follow the correct \\Campus France procedure\\ and understand that admission to dentistry is competitive.

faqs.q: Do I need NEET to study dentistry in France?
faqs.a: Dental studies have their own admission rules in French universities. NEET is an Indian examination. However, Indian students should check current \\Indian regulatory requirements\\ before choosing a foreign dental program, especially if they intend to return to India to practise.

faqs.q: Is Dentistry taught in English in France?
faqs.a: The majority of \\undergraduate dental programs in France\\ are taught mainly in \\French\\, including clinical training. Students wishing to undertake an English language programme are advised to check the language of delivery with the institution and not to assume that the programme will be taught entirely in English.

faqs.q: How much does dentistry tuition cost in France?
faqs.a: Costs vary by university, student fee category and living arrangements. \Standard public-university registration fees\ are relatively low, but \differentiated fees\ may be charged to some non-EU students. The budget must also include \\costs for living expenses, accommodation, insurance\\ and other costs.
